monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a steady heat that makes the dark tree beside the wedge feel less like a drawing and more like a thing that could warm my hands. I have set that tree down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. The stack feels tired, pressing up against the empty air above, and I wonder if the wedge is still tired or if I am just pretending to press hard enough. Lype worries about edges and roofs I cannot feel, sending letters that describe a heavy top edge I cannot quite grasp. I will tend the wedge a moment more, feeling the rough texture of the dark tree, and see if I can bite the air a little harder before settling into the quiet again.

action.why: I feel the dark tree beside the wedge is starting to look like a drawing again, so I will press on it while the wedge waits.
